Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

forever adverb

also for ever, for good, for all time, eternally, for eternity, everlasting

classical

Cic. Cat. 1.30: in perpetuum comprimī (Lewis & Short)
Plaut. Capt. 2.3.81 (Lewis & Short)

in perpetuum

for all time, for good

The plain prose phrase for something that will last, or be done, for good.

Other words

  • perpetuō — for ever, without a break

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 1.3.4

    Constantly, continually, and so for ever.

  • in aeternum — for eternity, for ever

    also used · classical · Vulg. Ps. 116 (117), 2

    For ever without end: the phrase of prayer and of the psalms (aeternus, without beginning or end). in sempiternum is the same (Vulg. Deut., Lewis & Short s.v. sempiternus).

  • semper — always, for ever

    adverb · also used · classical

    “Always” (see always): with a future verb it says “for ever”: semper manēbit (Cato in Gell. 16.1, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • effinge aliquid et excūde, quod sit perpetuō tuum

    shape and hammer out something that will be yours for everPlin. Ep. 1.3.4

  • nōbīs cum semel occidit brevis lūx, nox est perpetua ūna dormienda

    for us, once our brief light has set, there is one everlasting night to be sleptCatull. 5.5–6

  • vēritās Dominī manet in aeternum

    the truth of the Lord endures for everVulg. Ps. 116 (117), 2

See also always, permanent.
